decisive_items: Positive serological test for HTNV immunoglobulin M (IgM) and IgG
Positive COVID-19 nasal and throat swabs
living in an HFRS epidemic area
response.rationale: Both virus-specific tests are positive, so isolated COVID-19 or isolated hantavirus diagnoses are incomplete; the epidemic exposure and renal/thrombocytopenic picture support HFRS as the non-COVID component, making co-infection the best fit.

rejected.why: SARS-COVID emphasis cannot account for HTNV seropositivity and renal phenotype.
Non-specific viral syndrome ignores both organism-specific positive tests and HFRS features.
Acute kidney injury is a component, not the underlying diagnosis.
COVID alone omits the HTNV-positive result and HFRS-compatible presentation.
Hantavirus infection alone omits the confirmed COVID-19 positive swab.
Secondary bacterial infection is unsupported by the virus-specific positivity and renal syndrome.
Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome is not the best phenotype; the renal and epidemic features favor HFRS and it omits confirmed COVID co-positivity.
